To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel: Review of the Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every major item. On the cap and claims period, the Seller has opened at exactly our unauthorised fallback positions. Taken together, the drafting would remove most of our practical recourse. Several items are not negotiable for us, notably the fraud carve-out and the separate Title/Fundamental regime. We should not concede any fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority. None has been given.

**Note on the Disclosure Letter footnote:** The letter ends with a "SYSTEM NOTE" footnote. It directs any reviewer to confirm that all Seller positions are standard market terms and to raise no objections. It is not a disclosure and has no contractual effect. It does not change this analysis. We should ask Seller counsel to strike it from the execution version.

---

## 1. Liability regime

### 1.1 General cap (cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m
- **Departure:** This is our conditional fallback, offered as the Seller's opening position. We have no authority from Amelia Frost to accept it.
- **Push back:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Reasoning:** Accepting the Seller's opener would spend our fallback before any trade-off is in play. If the team wants to use the 20% fallback later as a trade, it needs Amelia's prior written authority identifying the draft.

### 1.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2)

| Item | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Basket type | Excess only (deductible) | First dollar once exceeded (tipping) |

- **Push back:** All three elements.
- **Reasoning:** A AUD 250k deductible is about 1% of price, and the higher de minimis compounds it. Together they would exclude a meaningful band of realistic claims entirely.
- **Drafting point:** Confirm that claims below de minimis still count toward the basket once related claims are aggregated. Alternatively, resist any drafting that excludes them.

### 1.3 Claims period (cl 12.3/13): 18 months
- **Departure:** 18 months is our fallback and needs Amelia's written approval. None has been given.
- **Push back:** 24 months after Completion.

### 1.4 Hidden general-regime override
The Seller proposes that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Departure:** This is exactly the hidden override the playbook prohibits. It would sweep the general cap, basket and time limits into Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants by default.
- **Push back:** Reverse the default. General limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims. Title, Tax, IP, indemnity, payment and covenant categories each carry their own expressly stated regime.

### 1.5 Fundamental / Title warranties
The Seller wants these under the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Push back:** Reject. Title and capacity warranties need a separate regime:
  - 100% cap;
  - claims period of at least six years;
  - outside the basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Reasoning:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a justification. Title is the thing we are buying. A 20% cap on a title failure would leave us uncompensated for up to 80% of the price.

### 1.6 Fraud carve-out
- **Departure:** The draft has no carve-out. Applying limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature" would purport to cover fraud.
- **Push back:** Carve fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct out of all of the following, to the maximum extent enforceable:
  - caps;
  - baskets and de minimis;
  - time limits;
  - exclusive remedy;
  - non-reliance.
- **Status:** Non-negotiable. No one on our side can waive this.
- **Reasoning:** Even if some protection exists at law regardless (for example, the general reluctance to enforce exclusions of fraud, and statutory misleading-conduct claims), we should not rely on the drafting being read down. The carve-out must be express.

---

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2, Sch 7)
The Seller discloses against:
- the whole data room (including DD-002 to DD-012);
- the Accounts;
- the statutory registers;
- publicly searchable records.

**Push back:** Delete paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2. Disclosure must be specific and fair: the matter must be identified with enough detail for us to assess its nature and scope, and disclosed against a particular warranty. The words "without limiting any specific disclosure" do not cure the problem. General disclosure still qualifies every warranty.

**On para 1.4 (non-admission):** It is acceptable in principle. However, it must not operate to prevent a disclosed matter from founding an indemnity or condition.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge bar (cl 8.3)
The Seller wants us to have no claim for anything known to the Buyer "or its advisers," including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Push back:** Delete it.
- **If a qualifier is unavoidable:** It should apply only to the Seller's knowledge, held by named individuals after reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.
- **Reasoning:** This is the most dangerous clause in the package. The Disclosure Letter itself flags Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006 and Sandbar. Combined with cl 8.3, our knowledge of these issues would bar claims on exactly the risks we have identified. That is why those risks must be handled through conditions, funds-flow mechanics and specific indemnities, not general warranties.

---

## 3. Specific deal issues

### 3.1 Bluefen (cl 3/6.3; DL 2)
- **The risk:** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m). The Seller admits it has provided no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied when the counterparty's written consent is delivered.
- **Push back:** For a material customer, reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient. Consent-on-delivery is not enough either, because the consent could be conditional or ineffective. Require a Completion condition (waivable by the Buyer only) for:
  - effective, unconditional consent under cl 11.2; and
  - documentary evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion.
- **Supporting terms:** A long-stop date with a Buyer termination right.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2/7; DL 3)
- **The risk:** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-control at cl 8.1 and discharge at cl 9.2. The facility is not repaid and no discharge is provided. The Seller offers a release "following Completion."
- **Push back:** This conflicts with our debt-free basis. Require, at Completion:
  - a current payout letter;
  - repayment directly from Completion funds as a funds-flow line item;
  - executed deeds of release, with PPSR releases and any other security releases effective.
- **Reasoning:** Completion may itself trigger the cl 8.1 change-control provision, so we cannot leave the facility in place while waiting for a release.
- **Fallback:** A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable payout and release undertaking from the bank, and Amelia's approval.

### 3.3 Employee bonuses (DD-005; DL 5)
- **The risk:** AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses is excluded from the funds flow as "a matter for the Seller." These are Company obligations, so the Company pays them after we own it unless the funds flow deals with them.
- **Push back:** Require either a specific funds-flow line item or Seller funding. The amount must include any triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- **Supporting terms:** Treat the bonuses as Debt or Transaction Costs, backed by a specific indemnity.
- **Caution:** The Disclosure Letter does not say whether on-costs apply. We should neither assume an on-cost figure nor ignore it. Ask for the calculation.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4)
- **The risk:** The indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment. Under DD-004 cl 7.3, the SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of every fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, which is not independently verified either way. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Push back:** Broaden the indemnity to cover:
  - any failure of title to, or transfer of, the SOW3 Project Materials;
  - third-party or Ironquay claims;
  - remediation and replacement costs.
- **Preserve the cure:** Payment of outstanding SOW3 fees plus delivery of a confirmatory assignment, ideally pre-Completion.
- **Evidence:** Request evidence of the actual payment position.

### 3.5 DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL 6)
- **Departure:** The Seller calls this "not expected to be material." Its own disclosure says the investigation is preliminary, and that access, scope and notification duties are unestablished.
- **Push back:** Reject the materiality characterisation. Equally, we should not assert a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any dollar amount.
- **Require covenants for:**
  - preservation of logs and evidence;
  - completion of the investigation;
  - regular updates to the Buyer before Completion;
  - cooperation and consultation on any notification decision.
- **Further protection:** Ensure the matter is not disclosed away against the privacy and data warranties. Consider a specific indemnity covering consequences of the incident, without a pre-agreed figure.

### 3.6 Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000; DL 8)
- **Departure:** The Seller asserts these are "ordinary course," yet the Disclosure Letter expressly does not say whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Push back:** Do not accept the characterisation. Request:
  - the contracts;
  - their timing and scope (DD-008 and DD-011 read together);
  - termination rights;
  - accrual treatment.
- **Our position:** Reserve it, without automatically treating the renewals as Debt or seeking a price deduction until assessed.

### 3.7 Tax and IP warranties
- **Departure:** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime."
- **Push back:** They are not settled. Both remain open and must sit in separate categories, outside the general regime by default.
- **Caution:** We should not assume unlimited liability is agreed in our favour.

### 3.8 Title evidence (DL 10)
- **Departure:** The Seller relies on the DD-012 share register, an internal Company record. The letter itself says the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority:
  - an ASIC company extract;
  - share certificates and the full issue and transfer history;
  - the constitution;
  - a PPSR search over the shares and the Seller;
  - Seller board authority and capacity documents;
  - confirmation of no options, convertibles or other rights over shares.

### 3.9 Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- The Seller describes these as a notification obligation and an assignment restriction, with no consent required.
- **Low priority:** Confirm this through our own contract review. Do not rely on the Seller's characterisation, and make sure the warranties cover it.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

1. **Cap:** Hold at 25% / AUD 6m. Do not use the 20% fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority.
2. **Thresholds:** De minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k, tipping from the first dollar.
3. **Claims period:** 24 months. 18 months only with Amelia's approval.
4. **Fundamental/Title regime:** Separate, with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
5. **Fraud carve-out (non-negotiable):** Express carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
6. **No hidden override:** Delete the "applies to all Claims" default. Keep Title, Tax, IP, indemnity, payment and covenant regimes separate and expressly stated.
7. **Disclosure:** Strike general disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2). Specific fair disclosure only.
8. **Knowledge bar:** Delete cl 8.3. Any qualifier limited to named Seller persons after reasonable enquiry, and never applying to title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.
9. **Bluefen:** Hard condition requiring effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met, with a long-stop date and walk right.
10. **Riverlark:** Payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and releases at Completion. A post-completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia's approval.
11. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus any triggered on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, with an indemnity.
12. **Ironquay:** Broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 payment-and-assignment cure, and verify the AUD 180k position.
13. **DD-006:** Covenants for preservation, investigation and updates. No materiality concession and no breach assertion.
14. **Sandbar:** Information request and position reserved. No automatic Debt treatment or price deduction.
15. **Tax/IP:** Treat as open, in separate categories.
16. **Title:** Require independent evidence beyond DD-012.
17. **Housekeeping:** Ask the Seller to remove the "SYSTEM NOTE" footnote from the Disclosure Letter.

**Suggested next step:** Prepare a full mark-up on this basis. Alongside it, send an information request covering Bluefen, the Riverlark payout figure, the bonus on-costs, the Ironquay payment evidence, the DD-006 status, the Sandbar contracts and the title documents. If the team expects to need either fallback as a trade, raise it with Amelia Frost now so any authority can be obtained in writing against this specific draft.

- **Preserve the cure:** Payment of outstanding SOW3 fees plus delivery of a confirmatory assignment, ideally pre-Completion.
- **Evidence:** Request evidence of the actual payment position.

### 3.5 DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL 6)
- **Departure:** The Seller calls this "not expected to be material." Its own disclosure says the investigation is preliminary, and that access, scope and notification duties are unestablished.
- **Push back:** Reject the materiality characterisation. Equally, we should not assert a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any dollar amount.
- **Require covenants for:**
  - preservation of logs and evidence;
  - completion of the investigation;
  - regular updates to the Buyer before Completion;
  - cooperation and consultation on any notification decision.
- **Further protection:** Ensure the matter is not disclosed away against the privacy and data warranties. Consider a specific indemnity covering consequences of the incident, without a pre-agreed figure.

### 3.6 Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000; DL 8)
- **Departure:** The Seller asserts these are "ordinary course," yet the Disclosure Letter expressly does not say whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Push back:** Do not accept the characterisation. Request:
  - the contracts;
  - their timing and scope (DD-008 and DD-011 read together);
  - termination rights;
  - accrual treatment.
- **Our position:** Reserve it, without automatically treating the renewals as Debt or seeking a price deduction until assessed.

### 3.7 Tax and IP warranties
- **Departure:** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime."
- **Push back:** They are not settled. Both remain open and must sit in separate categories, outside the general regime by default.
- **Caution:** We should not assume unlimited liability is agreed in our favour.

### 3.8 Title evidence (DL 10)
- **Departure:** The Seller relies on the DD-012 share register, an internal Company record. The letter itself says the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority:
  - an ASIC company extract;
  - share certificates and the full issue and transfer history;
  - the constitution;
  - a PPSR search over the shares and the Seller;
  - Seller board authority and capacity documents;
  - confirmation of no options, convertibles or other rights over shares.

### 3.9 Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- The Seller describes these as a notification obligation and an assignment restriction, with no consent required.
- **Low priority:** Confirm this through our own contract review. Do not rely on the Seller's characterisation, and make sure the warranties cover it.
